rounds.text: Juniper Green Energy Ltd is demonstrating explosive top-line acceleration that far outpaces broader sector norms, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 29% and a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 41% [E14, E15], alongside a screen-noted year-over-year sales surge of 114% [E54]. This top-line momentum translates directly into extraordinary operational profitability, highlighted by an operating margin of 85% in March 2026 that expanded by 4 percentage points over three years [E21], and a quarterly operating margin reaching 91% in September 2026 with an increasing trend over the last four quarters [E22, E24]. Crucially, the business exhibits elite cash conversion with operating cash flow hitting Rs 470 Cr in March 2026, delivering an 11.75x cash conversion ratio against reported profit that confirms profits are fully backed by hard cash [E25, E26]. Furthermore, insider and institutional confidence remains exceptionally secure with promoters holding an overwhelming 85.94% stake as of September 2026 [E32], and the company maintains historical price stability with a remarkably low peak-to-trough drawdown of just -17.7% [E43]. Conceded: [E27, E28, E36].

Juniper Green Energy Ltd carries severe valuation and fundamental risks that are completely disconnected from its underlying performance. The stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 230x and an EV/EBITDA of 26.77x, both of which tower far above their respective sector benchmarks of 19.43x and 10.18x [E1, E6, E11]. This staggering premium is entirely unsupported by profitability, given that the company delivers an anemic ROE of 0.4% and an ROCE of just 3.3%, while trailing twelve-month profit growth has plummeted by -46% [E12, E13, E17]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at a mere Rs 29 per share against a market price of Rs 257, representing a staggering overvaluation margin of safety of -798.7% [E36, E37]. The balance sheet and cash generation reveal heavy structural vulnerabilities that exacerbate these valuation concerns. Free cash flow stands deeply negative at Rs -6,162 Cr in Mar 2026, and borrowings have expanded to Rs 14,806 Cr as of Sep 2026, driving the debt-to-equity ratio to a precarious 2.84x where total debt comfortably exceeds net worth [E27, E28, E30]. Additionally, the current ratio sits at 0.97x, indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets, while flagged risks explicitly warn of a low interest coverage ratio and potential capitalization of interest costs [E29, E50, E52]. Conceded: the company demonstrates robust top-line momentum with compounded sales growth over 3 years at 29% and a TTM figure of 41%, alongside an operating margin reaching 91% in Sep 2026 [E14, E15, E22]. However, this growth fails to translate into shareholder returns or safe coverage, leaving the current market price to unrealistically imply a 50.1% earnings growth rate against a base-case assumption of only 18.0% [E38].

Conceded: P/E and EV/EBITDA multiples stand high at 230x and 26.77x [E1, E11], and free cash flow is negative at Rs -6,162 Cr [E27]. However, the bear's focus on low historical ROE and profit retraction ignores explosive top-line momentum, with compounded sales growth reaching 41% over the trailing twelve months and quarterly sales showing a 114% year-on-year surge [E15, E54]. Operating margins are not just robust but expanding, hitting 91% in September 2026 with an increasing trend over the last four quarters [E22, E24]. This top-line strength converts into actual operating cash flow of Rs 470 Cr for March 2026, backed by a stellar 11.75x cash conversion rate where profits are fully supported by cash [E25, E26]. Furthermore, results are actively improving with a results score of 90 out of 100 and net profit growth hitting 41% year-on-year, demonstrating a strong turnaround that discounts stale sentiment [E56, E61]. Finally, the bear's worst-case drawdown risk is overstated given that the historical peak-to-trough drawdown is contained at just -17.7% [E43].

Conceded: trailing twelve months compounded sales growth reaches 41% and quarterly sales surged 114% year-on-year [E15, E54]. However, the bull's reliance on top-line expansion and a 91% operating margin in September 2026 [E22] completely glosses over a staggering -46% collapse in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17]. While operating cash flow hits Rs 470 Cr [E26], it is entirely dwarfed by an astronomical free cash flow deficit of Rs -6,162 Cr [E27] and total borrowings mounting to Rs 14,806 Cr [E30]. Conceded: the historical peak-to-trough drawdown is contained at -17.7% [E43]. Yet this limited price drop offers no fundamental protection against a burdensome debt-to-equity ratio of 2.84x, a current ratio of 0.97x where liabilities exceed assets [E28, E29], and a dismal 1% median return on equity across recent years [E18, E19, E20].
